name: Gang operations
summary: Thirty-nine gang-run sites can be raided for cash, narcotics, luxury watches and unique weapon variants.
body: PowerPyx counts them by owner: Kingfishers 3, Kolts & Associates 5, M7 2, La Polilla Negra 2, Final Chapter 4, San4San 5, PTT Youngin$ 2, The Guardia Brothers 3 and other criminals 13.
PowerPyx says a site shows a yellow icon and reads Robbery Opportunity until visited, counts as done only when every key valuable is taken, and later restocks so it can be hit again.
According to PowerPyx, 19 are marked through story progress, all 39 count for the completion checklist, and an extra PTT Youngin$ site comes with the Ultimate Edition.
Named sites in PowerPyx's list include Kingpin Bowling, Manatee Motel, Sunrise RV Park, M7 Compound, Casa Guardia and Farm Fix Meth Lab; its list was still incomplete at 32 of 39.

name: Bank jobs
summary: Twenty-two banks can be robbed: 14 small branches and 8 large banks that also have a vault.
body: PowerPyx says small banks open up partway through the third chapter and are complete once both the cash drawer and the safe are emptied.
PowerPyx lists branches of Fleeca, Shorefront and Lombank plus Gibson Brothers Bank and Druthers State Bank, with small-bank takes ranging from 5,000 to 45,000 dollars.
According to PowerPyx, bank cash comes as marked bills that need the Dye Pack Jammer before a fence will take them, and all 22 banks count for the completion checklist.

name: Bank vaults
summary: The eight large banks have vaults that can only be entered while a security van crew is making a delivery.
body: PowerPyx says the method is to tail a security van until it stops at a bank, then get into the vault while the guard's delivery holds it open.
PowerPyx gives takes of roughly 65,000 to 205,000 dollars per bank, the highest at two Lombank branches, and says the robbery brings an immediate four-star wanted level.
According to PowerPyx, vaults unlock through an optional job late in the fourth chapter, and Yasmani then sells van tips for 10,000 dollars once two payday loan stores have been robbed.
PowerPyx lists a trophy for robbing five vaults and says a vault job also satisfies the trophy for robbing an armored truck.

name: Payday loans
summary: Seven payday loan stores can be held up for counter cash and a back-room safe.
body: PowerPyx lists six in Vice-Dale County and one, Cash Flow, in Kelly County, with takes from 2,000 up to 25,000 dollars.
PowerPyx describes the job as threatening the teller, taking the cash from the counter, emptying the safe in the back and then losing the police.
According to PowerPyx they unlock at the same point as small banks, pay in marked bills, and all seven count for the completion checklist.

name: Smash 'n' grabs
summary: Thirty-five shops, 20 jewelry stores and 15 pawn shops, can be robbed by breaking display cases and cracking the back-room safe.
body: PowerPyx says pawn shops open up during the second chapter and jewelry stores during the third.
PowerPyx gives takes of 1,000 to 12,000 dollars for pawn shops and up to 25,000 dollars for the best jewelry stores, with the goods sold on to a fence.
According to PowerPyx, a store counts as done only once its safe is looted, and 34 of the 35 are needed for the completion checklist.
PowerPyx's trophy guide mentions a Snap Gun for entering a jewelry store by the back door unseen.

name: Stick ups
summary: Convenience stores, liquor stores and fast food outlets can be held up at gunpoint for the register cash.
body: PowerPyx's completion checklist counts 91 stick ups and asks for any 50.
PowerPyx's progress database instead lists 72 convenience stores, 14 liquor stores and 23 fast food outlets, which adds up to 109; the two PowerPyx pages do not agree.
PowerPyx lists Criminal challenges for robbing three stores in a day and two stores in each of the five counties within 20 minutes.

name: Fences
summary: Seven contacts buy stolen goods, each paying different rates for narcotics, jewelry, marked bills or cars.
body: PowerPyx lists Brian and Donnie in Key Lento early on, Moses and Dunk in Port Gellhorn, and Tyrone, Yasmani and Randy in Vice City.
According to PowerPyx, Tyrone pays best for narcotics, Yasmani pays best for jewelry and marked bills, Moses takes only cars without a tracker and Randy takes certain high-end cars.
PowerPyx says goods are dropped at a fence's container, and that garages later allow drop-offs to a chosen fence.
IGN says Brian's lockup is near the south-western tip of Key Lento, opened with the code 7700 at the keypad by the door, and the stash bag is sold at a yellow crate inside.

IGN says Donnie becomes a fence after the Chapter 1 mission Coming Home and pays more than Brian: his trailer is near the middle of Key Lento, north of the Nifty Threads Island Wear shop, the drugs go in a green crate at its tail end, and he pays by mail a little later.
IGN says fences buy three kinds of goods, Narcotics, Jewelry and Marked Bills, and hovering over a fence on the map shows what it pays for each.

IGN says the Key Lento fences are not available in Chapter 2, where Dunk's trailer, in a trailer park near Freedom Tattoo in Port Gellhorn, takes goods placed in his car's trunk and pays through BuckMe.

IGN says cars can only be sold once Moses Watkins has been met in Chapter 2; he takes untracked cars, hovering over his shop on the map shows a stolen car's sale price and its registration cost, and his texted requests for specific cars pay extra with a condition bonus.
IGN says pawn shops, marked by a green scales symbol, buy collectible cards and underwater treasures such as meteorites and doubloons; the nearest early one is in southern Hamlet.

name: Marked bills and the Dye Pack Jammer
summary: Cash from banks and payday loan stores is marked and has to be laundered through a fence using the Dye Pack Jammer.
body: PowerPyx says the jammer is obtained partway through the third chapter, at the point where bank and payday loan jobs open.
According to PowerPyx, fencing 250,000 dollars of marked bills counts for the completion checklist and for a trophy.

name: Selling stolen vehicles
summary: Stolen cars can be sold to different buyers depending on what kind of tracker they carry.
body: PowerPyx says Moses in Port Gellhorn buys cars with no tracker, Pay 'n' Spray shops (19 in all) take cars with a standard tracker from the third chapter, and Randy buys wish-list cars with advanced trackers once the Key Cloner is available.

PowerPyx's money guide puts typical prices at 1,000 dollars or more from Moses, around 4,000 dollars at a Pay 'n' Spray and 30,000 dollars or more for a wish-list car in perfect condition; Randy's list has 18 cars.
According to PowerPyx, 200,000 dollars of vehicle sales counts for the completion checklist.

name: Robbery types
summary: The game's progress menu groups robberies into 11 kinds, from store stick ups to bank vaults.
body: PowerPyx's database heading gives 11 types but itemises seven: convenience stores, liquor stores, fast food joints, jewelry stores, pawn shops, payday loans and bank jobs.
Gang operations appear under the same Robberies map filter as Illegal Operations, according to PowerPyx.
GameSpot says safe codes are randomised: they differ between players and change even when the same shop is robbed twice, so published code lists do not help.

GameSpot says a code may be found on a guard or nearby, and in banks on sticky notes, computer screens or downed guards; without one, small safes can be picked and lockboxes snapped open with the Snap Gun, and nearly all safes can be forced.
GameSpot says the Snap Gun, unlocked through the story, opens locked doors without setting off the alarm, and that once the alarm panel is switched off, displays can be smashed without triggering it.
GameSpot says bank vaults cannot be picked or blown open; they open only briefly when an armoured cash truck delivers, and Yasmani, a fence met in Chapter 3, sells tips on where the trucks are.
